extraction.name: Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks
extraction.description: Paper introducing U-TAE and PaPs for semantic and panoptic segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series, and presenting the PASTIS dataset with panoptic annotations for agricultural parcels.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot; Loic Landrieu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PASTIS was built from open-access Sentinel-2 satellite image time series and parcel annotations from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). The authors stacked all available acquisitions for selected patches between September 2018 and November 2019, and used the parcel extents and crop types reported by farmers in FLPIS.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some acquisitions were automatically filtered out by the satellite data provider due to extensive cloud cover. Parcels whose surface was more than 50% outside of a patch were annotated with the void label. Some patches are partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-access Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery from four Sentinel-2 tiles in France, and parcel extent/content annotations from the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The 13 Sentinel-2 spectral bands were reduced to 10 by excluding atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10. Images were atmospheric-corrected and resampled to 10 meters per pixel. Parcels were cropped to patch extent, bounding boxes were adjusted accordingly, and parcels with more than 50% outside the patch were assigned the void label.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Acquisitions with extensive cloud cover were automatically filtered by the provider. The dataset was left as raw data without further cloud detection or preprocessing. Sequences were padded with all-zero images during training to handle variable lengths, with a padding mask used to exclude padded values from encoding and temporal averages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel was assigned a semantic label corresponding to a crop type or background, and each non-background pixel also received a unique instance label. Parcel-level annotations included crop type, pixel-precise mask, bounding box, and instance index. The crop annotations were taken from FLPIS and were estimated by the French Payment Agency to have over 98% accuracy via in situ control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset uses a void label for parcels outside the nomenclature or with insufficient overlap with the patch. Predicted parcels overlapping void parcels with IoU greater than 0.5 are ignored in metrics, following the panoptic evaluation protocol. The paper also notes a metric correction for Recognition Quality (RQ) due to a bug in the original implementation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 semantic label and 1 instance label per non-background pixel; parcel-level annotations also include one crop type, one bounding box, and one binary instance mask per parcel.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Farmers reported parcel extent and content in FLPIS; no further annotator demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: PASTIS and the implementation are publicly available on GitHub. The paper does not specify a formal versioning, update schedule, maintainer policy, or deprecation policy.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography/location of agricultural parcels and geo-referencing metadata are included. No direct human personal attributes are collected.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that crop mapping and parcel monitoring have major economic and environmental implications, including fair allocation of agricultural subsidies and ensuring crop rotation practices are respected. It also mentions applications such as surveying urban development and deforestation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. Patches were selected to favor rare crop types, and the dataset spans four regions of France, which may limit representativeness beyond those regions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains irregular temporal sampling and partial cloud cover. Some parcels are thin, fragmented, or have ambiguous borders, making panoptic segmentation difficult. The paper notes that mono-temporal inference performs poorly and that the dataset is focused on agricultural parcels in France, limiting generalization.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, testing, and cross-validation for semantic segmentation and panoptic segmentation of satellite image time series. The dataset is also used for benchmarking crop type classification and parcel delineation.
